children: , the health-insurance and services giant, dropped approximately 1.1% to $396.31 Friday as investors sized up a major bet on less healthcare bureaucracy. Starting October 1, UnitedHealthcare will eliminate 30% of its prior-authorization requirements across most commercial, Medicare Advantage, community and individual-exchange plans.

The upside is obvious: fewer forms, faster treatment decisions and lower administrative costs. But UnitedHealth has little margin for error. UnitedHealthcare generated $86 billion in second-quarter revenue but only $3.9 billion in operating profita slim 4.5% margin. The broader company delivered $112 billion in revenue, $8 billion in operating earnings and $11.1 billion in operating cash flow.

This is where the story gets serious. Removing approval barriers could make the insurance machine faster and cheaperor send claims costs climbing if utilization jumps. At $396.31, the stock sits 33.11% below its $592.44 GF Value, suggesting a massive valuation gap. Closing it will require proof that UnitedHealth can cut paperwork without cutting deeper into profits.

title: UnitedHealth Falls as 30% of Approval Barriers Vanish
